summary.text: A nucleotide is a molecule made of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate.
Nucleotides are the single units that link up to form the nucleic acid chains of DNA and RNA.
Beyond building DNA and RNA, nucleotides supply chemical energy in cells and take part in cell signaling.

facts.label: Three parts
facts.value: A nucleobase, a five-carbon sugar and a phosphate group

facts.label: Energy carriers
facts.value: ATP, GTP, CTP and UTP provide chemical energy

facts.label: Where they come from
facts.value: Obtained in the diet and made by the liver

facts.label: In food
facts.value: 5-nucleotides are additives that boost umami taste

items.prompt: A label calls a molecule a nucleoside triphosphate. What does that name tell you?

options.label: It contains three separate sugar rings
It carries three different nucleobases
Its phosphate group is made up of three phosphates
It is joined to three other nucleotides

items.explain: A nucleotide is called a mono-, di- or triphosphate depending on how many phosphates make up its phosphate group.

items.prompt: You remove the phosphate from a nucleotide. What is left?

options.label: The sugar and the nucleobase together, called a nucleoside
Only the nucleobase, because the sugar leaves too
Only the sugar, because bases are held separately
A short nucleic acid made of two sugars

items.explain: The sugar and nucleobase together are called a nucleoside.

items.prompt: A nucleotide in a cell has the sugar ribose. What is it called?

options.label: A deoxyribonucleotide
A nucleoside triphosphate only
A nucleobase
A ribonucleotide

items.explain: Nucleotides are termed ribonucleotides if the sugar is ribose and deoxyribonucleotides if it is deoxyribose.

items.prompt: In a double helix the two strands run in opposite directions. What does that allow?

options.label: Each strand to be built with no phosphate groups
Base pairing and complementarity between the strands
Nucleotides to swap sugars between the strands
The strands to hold completely different base sets

items.explain: The opposite orientation permits base pairing and complementarity, which is essential for copying and reading the encoded information.

items.prompt: Cells need chemical energy for many jobs. Which nucleotides supply it?

options.label: Nucleobases alone, with no sugar or phosphate
Cyclic nucleotides such as cAMP and cGMP
Nucleoside triphosphates such as ATP and GTP
Cofactor nucleotides such as coenzyme A

items.explain: ATP, GTP, CTP and UTP provide chemical energy, while cyclic nucleotides handle signaling.

items.prompt: Cells do not only take nucleotides from food. Which organ is the major site of making them from scratch?

options.label: The liver, working from common nutrients
The stomach, working from swallowed protein
The lungs, working from inhaled gases
The skin, working from sunlight alone

items.explain: The liver is the major organ of de novo synthesis, and nucleotides are made from common nutrients.
